---
title: Muscle Guarding Reflex
---

Muscle guarding or "protective" peripheral motor reflexes (alpha and gamma motor neuron excitation) @tuckeyFCSF1Foundations2024




# He et al. 1988



He et al., sought out to determine if inflammation impacted increased &alpha;- and &gamma;- motor excitation to create muscle resistance to flexion/extension movements at a joint @heAcuteInflammationKnee1988.

- 1 cat (no humans)
- Controlled for voluntary motor control by anaesthetized cat
- Monitored &alpha; and &gamma;- motor neuron activity in the nerve to the biceps semitendinosus
- Performed Flexion/extension ROM of the knee joint
- Control: No acute inflammation added 
- Experimental:
    - Kaolin and carrageenan
- Results:

||&alpha;|&gamma;|
|-|-|-|
|n|44|84|
|Control (% responsive)|14%|41%|
|Experimental (Acute inflammation) (% responsive)|41%|64%|

Conclusion: acute inflammation decreased reflex thresholds for &alpha;- and &gamma;-motor neurons
